lines: I should get back to the vice and the anvil, where the work makes sense.
Best I finish polishing those edges before rust gets any ideas.
There are handles that still need balancing.
I promised a farmer a new hoe head by sunset.
<pulse>Back</pulse> to the stack of repairs before it grows taller.
I have filings to clear and bolts to check.
A tool keeps its edge only when someone cares for it.
I still need to test that new pattern properly.
I should get back before the workbench gets ahead of me.
I'll return to the shop, where metal answers best.
I need to finish a mattock before the light goes.
That is enough talking for now. My order book is not getting shorter.
I have a chisel cooling on the bench. I should check it.
The miller needs that wrench back before morning.
I had better sweep the filings before someone finds them with a bare hand.
There is a loose hammer head waiting for me.
I should oil the tools before I lock up.
A customer is waiting on a repaired pickaxe. I should finish it.
I have said my piece. The grindstone is next.
Come by later. I still have three handles to fit.
